_meta.description: The WebSocket frames between a Portico client (portico-app, the dashboard card, the panel) and the Portico integration, contract 3: one case per request, with every frame HA sends back in order, recorded from the integration's real handlers over a real Home Assistant websocket connection, with a fake door provider behind them. `as` is the caller: `phone` is an enrolled phone's dedicated HA user, `screen` a user declared for the dashboard endpoint `kitchen`, `user` an ordinary HA user (an administrator, an enrolled phone and a declared screen it is not), `admin` an administrator. `auth` is who may send each command (classes: admin, phone, dashboard, any; one table, custom_components/portico/auth.py); a caller outside a command's classes gets an `unauthorized` error (`not_enrolled` for portico/media_open). Message ids are per connection, as recorded. Errors with code invalid_format come from Home Assistant's own schema check; their message text is HA's and may change with HA versions. HA user ids are replaced by `user-<name>`, and `doc_rev` (a hash of a document that names HA user ids) by `<doc_rev>`; `content/save` is recorded only as a refusal and a stale save, because a good save changes the document.
_meta.consumers: portico-app's MockWebServer tests replay these frames; the card and panel node tests are written against the same shapes.
_meta.deterministic: reg_id comes from a counter instead of uuid4, the registry clock is fixed at 2026-10-06T10:00:00+00:00, the content rate limiter's clock is fixed; call ids and door ids come from the fake provider; everything else is as emitted.
_meta.fake_values: Every token, registration and id here is a fake test value.
_meta.producer: custom_components/portico/tests/test_ws_contract.py; regenerate with PORTICO_REGENERATE_WS_CONTRACT=1 (see that file). The test fails when this file drifts from the handlers.
